title: Settings save: render the dedicated SETTINGS_CRYPTO_UNAVAILABLE refusal instead of the generic error path
body:
Follow-up finding from objectstack-ai/objectstack#8273 (PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#8396), filed unassigned for triage.

As of that PR, the framework's fail-closed settings refusal — a declared-encrypted value (`encrypted: true` / manifest `type: 'password'`) refused because the deployment has nothing able to encrypt it — answers `PUT /api/settings/:namespace` with a dedicated wire envelope instead of the generic one:

- status: `500` (unchanged)
- `error.code`: `SETTINGS_CRYPTO_UNAVAILABLE` (was `INTERNAL_ERROR`)
- `error.details`: `{ namespace, key }` — the located refusal (never the value)
- `error.message`: unchanged; carries the operator prescription (wire `SettingsServicePluginOptions.cryptoProvider` or a real `crypto` adapter)

`SettingsView.tsx` already branches per code (`SETTINGS_LOCKED` is special-cased around line 152; `SETTINGS_VALIDATION` feeds the field-error extractor). `SETTINGS_CRYPTO_UNAVAILABLE` currently falls to the generic error path, which does surface the carried message — so nothing is broken; this is the client-side half the new code exists to enable: an admin saving a secret on a deployment that cannot encrypt should see "this deployment cannot encrypt secrets — reconfigure it" as a first-class state (pointing at the refused key via `error.details.key`), not a generic save failure.

Severity: low, enhancement-class. The framework half is done; nothing here blocks it.
